title: Washington Crossing the Delaware
source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (public domain: Leutze died in 1868). Wikimedia Commons: Washington Crossing the Delaware by Emanuel Leutze, MMA-NYC, 1851.jpg, 6004x3847.
caption: This famous painting is full of mistakes. How many can you spot? #art #arthistory #history #painting #museum
_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-11 (Wikipedia: 'Washington Crossing the Delaware (1851 painting)' and 'George Washington's crossing of the Delaware River'): painted in Düsseldorf, 1851, Met version; first version destroyed in Bremen 1942; Stars and Stripes first specified in the Flag Resolution of 14 June 1777, crossing was 25-26 Dec 1776; crossing started ~4-6 pm, artillery across by 3 am, weather drizzle -> rain -> sleet and snow; real Durham boats substantially larger; Fischer: everyone would have stood to avoid icy water in the bottom of the boat; river in background is the Rhine; man in Scottish bonnet and man of African descent next to each other; 1853 catalogue: James Monroe holds the flag.
'Losing and freezing' framing of the army in Dec 1776 is general history (low morale after defeats in New York), not from the sources above.

slides.headline: This famous painting is full of mistakes. Can you spot them?
slides.sub: Emanuel Leutze, Washington Crossing the Delaware, 1851

slides.headline: Christmas night, 1776
slides.text: The American army is beaten and freezing. Washington gambles: cross the icy Delaware and strike at dawn.

slides.headline: Mistake one: the flag
slides.text: The Stars and Stripes didn't exist yet. It was adopted in June 1777, six months later.

slides.headline: Mistake two: the light
slides.text: They really crossed in the dark, from evening until 3 a.m., through sleet and snow. No golden sunrise.

slides.headline: Mistake three: the boat
slides.text: The real ones were Durham boats: much bigger, with high sides. This little boat would barely hold them.

slides.headline: And that river?
slides.text: Leutze painted it in Düsseldorf, Germany. The water behind them is the Rhine.

slides.headline: Meanwhile, look at the crew
slides.text: A man in a Scottish bonnet. Beside him, a man of African descent. Leutze filled the boat with all kinds of Americans.

slides.headline: And holding the flag?
slides.text: According to the 1853 catalogue: James Monroe, the future fifth president.

slides.headline: But one 'mistake' isn't
slides.text: People say no one would stand in that boat. Historians say they all stood: the bottom was full of icy water.
